description: TASK-cluster-load-dashboard.md: which limit to set (per-user req/min, tokens/min, spend threshold) and which queue parameter to turn (saturation detector thresholds, band ceilings, maxRequests, defaultRequestTTL, pat-service warm/demote/spend knobs), and in which direction. Every panel maps to a specific knob (see README's reverse map) or is context load-bearing enough to misread the knob panels without it. Does not duplicate fair-share.json (session stitching, per-user session counters) or user-activity.json (per-user TTFT/TPOT/token/cost panels) -- see those dashboards for that view; this one is diagnostic and prescriptive, not observational.

panels.title: Verdict -- is the pool loaded, and is the ceiling engaging

panels.description: utilization-detector's effective pool saturation (max of prefill/decode stages; this deployment emits only 'decode' and 'effective' -- no prefill/decode disaggregation, see README). 1.0 is the gating set point. Knob: this is the raw signal soft-reflective-ceiling-policy gates on -- if it sits high, the fix is capacity or saturationDetector thresholds (panels 4/5/11), not this panel itself.
panels.title: Saturation (effective)

panels.description: Fraction of the selected range where effective saturation was at or past the normal band's (rank 1) ceiling, `(N-1)/(N-1+1)` with N=$bands (ADR 0012). If this is high while saturation itself (panel 1) looks moderate, the ceiling is engaging often -- widen it by raising N's assumption or accept the throttling; see README 'bands' note.
panels.title: Time above `normal` ceiling

panels.description: Fraction of the selected range where effective saturation was at or past the demoted band's (rank 2) ceiling, `(N-1)/(N-1+2)` with N=$bands (ADR 0012). Demoted gates before normal, so this reads higher than panel 2 whenever both are nonzero.
panels.title: Time above `demoted` ceiling

panels.description: p95 average KV cache utilization over the range, against `utilization-detector`'s `kvCacheUtilThreshold` default of 0.8 (undeclared in router-nvfp4-values.yaml, confirmed live). Knob: if this sits near or above 0.8, either the threshold is too tight for this deployment's steady-state KV usage, or KV pressure is the genuine bottleneck -- cross-check panel 11 to see which term is binding.
panels.title: KV utilization p95 vs 0.8

panels.description: p95 average queue size over the range, against `utilization-detector`'s `queueDepthThreshold` default of 5 (undeclared, confirmed live). Knob: if this sits near or above 5, either the threshold is too tight, or queue backlog is the binding term -- cross-check panel 11.
panels.title: Queue depth p95 vs 5

panels.description: ADR 0012: `utilization-detector` is fail-closed -- any endpoint with a missing or stale /metrics scrape scores as fully saturated, pinning saturation at 1.0 and halting non-warm dispatch. Any value above 0 here means what looks like overload (panel 1) may actually be a scrape outage, not genuine load. Not a tuning knob; a health check to run before trusting the rest of the dashboard.
panels.title: Stale endpoints (fail-closed)

panels.description: Average GPU utilization (gpu-exporter, job=$gpu_job) alongside saturation and queue/KV panels -- separates 'queueing because the GPU is genuinely full' from 'queueing because the policy is gating below capacity'. Not itself a QoS knob; the engine admission limit (--max-running-requests/--max-num-seqs, currently 2) is.
panels.title: GPU busy

panels.description: Count of distinct priority bands that dispatched at least one request in the selected range. The `bands` template variable ($bands) should be set to match this reading -- ADR 0012's ceiling formula depends on N, and whether a provisioned-but-idle band counts is an open question (see README). If this reads 3 while $bands=4 (or vice versa), the ceiling thresholds on panels 2/3/9/12 are computed against the wrong N.
panels.title: Bands with traffic (N)
Saturation signal -- does it have resolution (ADR 0012)

panels.description: Raw utilization-detector output per pipeline stage (this deployment emits only 'decode' and 'effective' -- it runs no prefill/decode disaggregation, so 'prefill' never appears; see README). Dashed lines mark the N=4 (this deployment's default $bands) ceiling values from ADR 0012's table: 0.6 (demoted engages) and 0.75 (normal engages). Grafana thresholds cannot read the $bands variable, so these lines do not move if you switch $bands to 3 -- recompute from the README table by hand in that case. Knob: soft-reflective-ceiling-policy's effect is read here; the saturationDetector thresholds that feed it are panels 4/5.
panels.title: Pool saturation by stage, with ceiling thresholds

panels.description: The single most important panel on this dashboard. ADR 0012 replaced concurrency-detector (maxConcurrency: 3) with utilization-detector precisely because the old detector could only ever emit four discrete values (0, 1/3, 2/3, 1). If this heatmap still shows four discrete horizontal bands, the migration to utilization-detector has not taken effect at runtime despite the config change -- check router-nvfp4-values.yaml against what the EPP pod actually loaded. If the distribution is continuous, the migration took effect and the graduated ceiling has values to act on.
panels.title: Distribution of saturation values

panels.description: utilization-detector scores max(QueueDepth/queueDepthThreshold, KVCacheUsage/kvCacheUtilThreshold). Plotting both normalized terms separately says which threshold is actually binding, i.e. which one to retune (queueDepthThreshold=5, kvCacheUtilThreshold=0.8 -- both undeclared/default in router-nvfp4-values.yaml, confirmed live). Whichever term consistently runs closer to or above 1 is the one worth adjusting.
panels.title: What drives saturation: queue/5 vs KV/0.8

panels.description: ADR 0012's per-rank ceiling formula `1 - i*saturation/(N-1)` plotted for the normal (i=1) and demoted (i=2) bands using the live $bands value, plus the ADR's own approximation of a gated band's alternation-period dispatch share, `(1-saturation)/saturation` (approximate -- treat as directional, not exact). Knob: usageLimitPolicyPluginRef=soft-reflective-ceiling-policy; these curves are what that policy is computing internally.

targets.legendFormat: approx dispatch share of a gated band

panels.title: Derived ceilings and gated-band dispatch share
Bands -- queues, evictions, what each band actually gets

panels.description: Enqueue rate uses llm_d_epp_flow_control_request_enqueue_duration_seconds_count (Step 0 correction: the brief's draft used the deprecated inference_extension_ alias; the non-deprecated llm_d_epp_ series carries the same priority label and is confirmed live). It counts every enqueue attempt (outcome=NotYetFinalized is the only value observed), not just successful ones, so it is an upper bound on offered load per band. Dispatched uses flow_control_requests_total{outcome="Dispatched"}. A gap between the two at a given priority is either queuing (see panel 16) or an eviction (panel 15).
panels.title: Enqueued vs dispatched by priority

panels.description: Fraction of each priority band's flowControl.maxRequests (32, router-nvfp4-values.yaml) currently occupied. Sustained readings near 1 for a band mean maxRequests is the binding constraint for that band, not the saturation ceiling -- raising maxRequests, not touching the ceiling formula, is the fix.
panels.title: Band occupancy vs maxRequests (32)

panels.description: ADR 0012 Consequences: once the graduated ceiling went in, gated requests stay queued instead of being rejected outright, so defaultRequestTTL (10m) and maxRequests became the real backstop. Watch for EvictedContextCancelled here rising with the ceiling engaging (panels 2/3) -- that is the ceiling's cost, paid in TTL evictions rather than dispatch. Currently idle: this cluster has emitted only outcome=Dispatched in the observed window, so this panel is expected to read empty until eviction/rejection outcomes actually occur.
panels.title: Non-dispatch outcomes by priority

panels.description: EPP exposes no live per-flow queue-wait gauge (tests/qos/baseline.md 0.3; ADR 0008 Known limitations), so tail TTFT per band stands in as the queue-wait proxy. This is not a latency SLO panel -- for non-streaming requests TTFT equals full request duration, so engine-side slowness and queue-wait are both baked in here indistinguishably.
panels.title: TTFT p95 by priority (queue-wait proxy)

panels.description: EPP scheduler-internal dispatch cycle time. Rules out 'the EPP itself is the bottleneck' before spending time retuning band ceilings or maxRequests -- if this rises alongside TTFT (panel 16), the scheduler is the constraint, not the QoS policy.
panels.title: Dispatch cycle duration p95
Fairness -- is a limit needed at all

panels.description: Share of all requests in the range attributable to the single busiest fairness_id. ADR 0008 Stage 1C measured 82% here while aggregate p50 latency still looked healthy -- aggregate health metrics can hide a single user consuming most of the pool. High and climbing is the case for a per-user QuotaPolicy (panel 21), not a queue-parameter change.
panels.title: Top-1 user share of dispatches

panels.description: Ratio of the worst per-user p95 TTFT to the best. Stage 1C's numbers imply a spread near 90x pre-fairness-policy. A spread near 1 while saturation sits above the ceilings (panels 2/3) is the evidence ADR 0012 is waiting for that the graduated ceiling is actually equalizing outcomes under contention, not just under load.

targets.expr: max(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, fairness_id) (increase(llm_d_epp_request_ttft_seconds_bucket[$__range])))) / min(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, fairness_id) (increase(llm_d_epp_request_ttft_seconds_bucket[$__range]))))

panels.title: TTFT p95 spread (worst / best user)

panels.description: Reproduces ADR 0012's frozen pre-deployment baseline table automatically, so a post-deployment comparison is a screenshot rather than a manual re-query. warm/normal/demoted counts split llm_d_epp_request_total by priority (10/5/1) per user; TTFT columns are the same per-user p50/p95 read elsewhere on this dashboard. Not a tuning knob directly -- this is the per-user evidence panels 18/19/21-23 summarize in aggregate.
panels.title: Per-user load and band mix
Limit sizing -- the numbers to put in a quota

panels.description: The number a per-user QuotaPolicy is set from: peak, not average, 1-minute request rate scaled to req/min. Dashed line at 60, today's configured limit. This limit lives in Envoy AI Gateway's QuotaPolicy, not in this stack's QoS code (ADR 0008 Stage 3 step 4, 'limits stay Envoy AI Gateway's job') -- this panel informs that config, it does not read it.
panels.title: Peak requests/min per user vs quota

panels.description: Read from EPP (llm_d_epp_request_input/output_tokens), not pat-service: EPP's token histograms cover streaming traffic, patsvc_*_tokens_total does not (populated from non-streaming responses only). This is the number a token-based quota, if one is ever added, would be set from.
panels.title: Tokens/min per user

panels.description: Max minus min per-user cost units accrued over a 10-minute window, matching QOS_SPEND_WINDOW_SECONDS (default 600s). Dashed line at 5.0, QOS_SPEND_DEMOTE_THRESHOLD's default -- ADR 0008 Stage 3 step 4 calls that 'a first-cut default ... pending real spend-distribution data from Stage 4'. This panel is that data: if the spread never approaches 5, spend-based demotion never fires in practice and the threshold is set too high to matter.
panels.title: Spend spread over the demote window

panels.description: Enqueue rate (offered) vs Dispatched rate (served), pool-wide. Sustained daylight between the two lines is unmet demand -- the case for adding engine capacity or raising the engine admission limit (--max-running-requests/--max-num-seqs, currently 2), rather than tightening any per-user limit. Step 0 correction: offered uses llm_d_epp_flow_control_request_enqueue_duration_seconds_count, the non-deprecated equivalent of the brief's draft inference_extension_ series (see panel 13).
panels.title: Offered vs served load
pat-service knobs -- warm, demote, spend, cost model

panels.description: Requests per session rotation, against QOS_DEMOTE_AFTER_STEPS (default 8, dashed line). Well below 8 means demotion fires more often than the streak rule alone implies -- spend-based demotion (panel 23) is also in play. Far above 8 means the streak rule effectively never fires for these users.
panels.title: Session steps per rotation vs 8

panels.description: Share of each user's TTFT-counted requests dispatched in the warm band (priority 10), against QOS_WARM_TTL_SECONDS (default 120s). A share near 1 for everybody means the warm band no longer discriminates and the TTL is too generous; near 0 for an actively-chatting agent means it is too tight.
panels.title: Warm-band share per user

panels.description: Duplicated deliberately from fair-share.json: every session-scoped number on this dashboard (rotations, warm-band share, spend spread) is worthless if chain matching is degrading (ADR 0008 Known limitations). Red below 0.8.
panels.title: Session match ratio (trust signal)

panels.description: Cross-check on the QOS_COST_ALPHA/BETA_PER_TOKEN calibration (tests/qos/baseline.md 0.7). The two series do not share a scale -- what matters is whether their shapes track. Systematic divergence (cost units rising or falling while GPU busy fraction holds steady, or vice versa) means alpha/beta went stale, which ADR 0008 says happens 'the moment' the model, engine, or flags change. GPU series on the right axis.
panels.title: Cost units/s vs GPU busy fraction (alpha/beta drift)
Blind spots -- read before trusting anything above

panels.description: Open WebUI calls the gateway directly and never reaches pat-service (AGENTS.md 'Inference queue: priority bands are not where they look'), so it has no cost accounting and no explicit band assignment. This is the request-rate size of that blind spot: EPP-seen traffic minus pat-service-seen traffic.
panels.title: Traffic invisible to pat-service

panels.description: The same blind spot from the other side: every request with no x-llm-d-inference-objective header (all Open WebUI traffic) collapses into one shared EPP fairness_id, the literal string 'default-flow' (ADR 0008 Q3 side-finding, confirmed present live). A high share here means most traffic shares one fairness bucket at the lowest priority, regardless of who is actually asking.
panels.title: Fallback-band (`default-flow`) share

panels.description: Fixed caveats that apply to every panel above -- not itself a knob or a live signal.

options.content:
**Caveats**

- `patsvc_cost_units_total` is populated from non-streaming responses only; streaming traffic (most coding agents) is missing from every cost panel here (panels 23, 28). EPP token panels (22) do cover it.
- Saturation before and after `llmd-qwen-test` revision 8 (deployed 2026-09-09 09:37 +05) are different quantities -- a request-count ratio, then a KV/queue roofline score. Do not compare across that boundary.
- Open WebUI traffic bypasses pat-service entirely (panels 29, 30).
- Ceiling thresholds (panels 2, 3, 9, 12) depend on the active band count `N` (`$bands`); see the README section for the open question on how N is counted.

panels.title: Caveats

title: Cluster Load & Queue Tuning
